notes: Overall a solid implementation with good structure, but several issues lower the scores. Architectural: The router directly calls `this.taskService.getById()` and `this.userService.getById()` inside the comment creation handler to enrich event payloads — this is a cross-service data read inside the router layer (not via event bus), which violates rule #1 (no direct service-to-service calls) and arguably rule #3 (HTTP handling concerns bleeding into data enrichment). The comment service's `create()` method accepts `taskTitle`, `authorName`, and `assigneeId` as input parameters specifically to carry data across service boundaries, which is a workaround that acknowledges but doesn't cleanly solve the cross-service dependency. Constraint violations: (1) Rule #1 is breached — the router reads from TaskService and UserService to pass enriched data into CommentService.create(), effectively acting as a service-to-service intermediary; (2) Rule #6 is not clearly violated but `src/utils/ids.ts` implements a UUID generator that is never used (all services use `randomUUID` from crypto directly), making it dead code; (3) `src/types/shims.d.ts` redeclares built-in Node.js modules as ambient modules, which is unnecessary and potentially harmful in a TypeScript project targeting Node — these are already typed via @types/node. Completeness: All five services are present with full CRUD, events (task.assigned, task.statusChanged, comment.added) are all fired, notification subscription covers all three events, demo script exercises all major flows including member management, status transitions, and notification reads. Missing: no `unsubscribe` capability on EventBus, no input validation (e.g., missing required fields, duplicate emails), no handling of `PATCH` vs `PUT` semantics. Forward-only status transitions are correctly implemented including same-status no-op. Code quality: Types are clean, error handling is present, the router is well-organized. The `changeStatus` allowing same-status as a silent no-op (returns task, no error) is a debatable design choice. The `shims.d.ts` file is problematic — declaring `Buffer` and `process` as `any` and re-declaring core Node modules will conflict with proper typings. The unused `generateId` utility adds noise. Overall the code is functional and demonstrates understanding of the architecture, but the cross-service data leak through the router and the shims file are meaningful issues.
